goal: SnipMD phase 2: storage foundation (SPEC §6.1 atomic writes and encoding, §6.1 write failure, §7 session writes and restore)

signatures.doc: snipmd_core::atomic. Creates a temp file next to the target (same folder, name `.<file name>.<unique>.tmp`, opened with create_new; unique part from process id, an atomic counter and the time, no new crates), writes all bytes, sync_all, closes it, then fs::rename over the target. On any error the temp file is removed and the error returned; the target is never truncated or partly written. Never creates missing folders: a missing parent is an error (SPEC §6.1 write failure).

signatures.signature: pub fn decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(String, TextFormat), TextError>; pub fn encode(text: &str, fmt: TextFormat) -> Vec<u8>
signatures.doc:
snipmd_core::text. decode: format from sniff; strips a UTF-8 BOM; converts every 
 to 
 (a lone  stays); invalid UTF-8 is TextError::NotUtf8. encode: normalizes 
 to 
 first, then writes 
 line breaks when fmt.crlf, and a BOM when fmt.bom. encode(decode(b)) == b for any file whose line breaks are all of one kind.

snipmd_core::text. Never fails, also for non-UTF-8 bytes. bom = starts with EF BB BF. crlf = the first line break is \r\n; a file without any line break counts as crlf (new and one-line files get the Windows default, SPEC §6.1). TextFormat::default() stays {crlf:false,bom:false}; add `pub const NEW_FILE: TextFormat = TextFormat { crlf: true, bom: false };` for new notes.

signatures.signature: #[tauri::command] read_markdown_file(path) -> Result<String, String>; #[tauri::command] write_markdown_file(path, content) -> Result<(), String>; #[tauri::command] save_session(json) -> Result<(), String>
signatures.doc: Unchanged names and payloads. read: fs::read, then text::decode; NotUtf8 becomes "<name> is not UTF-8 text". write: the format of the file on disk now (text::sniff of its bytes) or text::NEW_FILE when it does not exist; any other read error is returned; then text::encode and atomic::atomic_write. No create_dir_all for notes. save_session: atomic_write of session.json (creating the app data folder stays).

src/session.ts. Cancels a pending debounce, queues a write of the current snapshot now and resolves when that write (and every write queued before it) has finished, also when it failed (the failure is reported through showError as today). Never rejects.

signatures.signature: export async function saveTab(id: string): Promise<boolean>; export async function flushDirty(): Promise<void>
signatures.doc: src/saving.ts, same signatures as today. Writes of one tab never overlap: a per-tab chain runs them in order, so the last write carries the newest text. flushDirty starts flushSession() at once (the session never waits for a note write), writes every dirty disk tab in parallel, then awaits flushSession() again so the saved flags land in the session; resolves when all of that settled and never rejects. A failed write leaves only that tab dirty and shows `showError('save <title>', err)`; a later successful write of that tab dismisses its error bar.

Tests in src-tauri/core/tests/atomic.rs and src-tauri/core/tests/text.rs. atomic: a new target is created; an existing target is replaced completely (shorter content leaves no tail); when the rename fails (make the target an existing non-empty directory) the call errs, the directory is untouched and no `.tmp` file is left in the folder; a missing parent folder errs and creates nothing; two writes in a row leave exactly the second content. text: LF, CRLF, BOM+CRLF, BOM+LF and empty files round-trip byte for byte through decode/encode; a file without line breaks sniffs as crlf; non-UTF-8 bytes are NotUtf8 for decode while sniff still answers; encode with crlf of text that already contains \r\n does not double it; a lone \r survives decode.

units.task: Session writes and restore (SPEC §7). (1) src/session.ts: add T2b flushSession exactly as the contract says; keep scheduleSessionSave, the 500 ms debounce, the serial write queue and the identical-snapshot skip. (2) src/tabs.ts, only snapshot() and restore(): snapshot() returns copies of the tabs and never changes a tab's in-memory content (a restored tab that was never shown has no EditorState and lives on tab.content); in the copies, a clean disk-backed tab (filePath set, dirty false) gets content '' because the disk is its source, while untitled and dirty tabs carry their text. restore() reads every clean disk-backed tab from disk with readNote in parallel (Promise.allSettled) before any editor is created and puts the text in tab.content; a tab whose read fails is dropped and one showError('reopen <names>', <first reason>) names all of them; when no tab is left it opens a new untitled tab; the active tab falls back to the first remaining one. Dirty disk tabs keep their session text (the conflict check is phase 4). Do not change anything else in tabs.ts. Tests: extend src/session.test.ts (vi.mock './ipc' and './infobar'; fake timers): an immediate save calls saveSessionRaw without waiting 500 ms (the paste path), several debounced calls inside 500 ms write once, flushSession resolves only after saveSessionRaw resolved, resolves (does not reject) when it rejected, and a failed write of a snapshot is retried by the next save of the same snapshot. Write src/tabs.test.ts (vi.mock './ipc', './infobar', './preview/render' and the titlebar; jsdom): snapshot gives '' for a clean disk tab, the text for dirty and untitled tabs, and leaves tab.content of the live tabs unchanged; restore takes a clean tab's text from readNote, not from the session; a failing read drops that tab, keeps the others and shows one error.
units.output: session.ts with flushSession; tabs.ts snapshot/restore; session.test.ts extended; tabs.test.ts; checks passing.

units.task: Adversarial review of the phase 2 diff (git diff HEAD) against SPEC.md §6.1 and §7 and the CLAUDE.md data-safety guardrails 1, 5 and 6 and the code conventions. Hunt for: a path where a note or session.json can end truncated or half-written; a temp file left behind or created in another folder (cross-drive rename); a line-ending or BOM change on save of an existing note; a write that creates a deleted folder again; a note write that can delay or block the session write or another tab; overlapping writes of one tab that let older text win while the tab shows clean; snapshot() losing the text of a tab that was never shown; restore() trusting the session copy of a clean tab; a close (Alt+F4) that ends before the session write; the info bar hiding or duplicating errors; anything that breaks phase 0/1 behaviour (open, save, paste, session restore, the allowed-set checks).
